explanation: Sine and cosine are the same wave shifted by a quarter period: cos x is just sin x started a quarter-turn earlier, which is why cos starts at its peak and sin starts at 0. The amp slider sets the amplitude A — the height of the peaks above and below the midline — and the readout prints the live y-values as the sweeping dot rides the curve. Use the which slider to show sine only, cosine only, or both together so you can line up their peaks and zeros.
bullets: Both have period 2π and oscillate between +A and −A about the midline y = 0.
cos x = sin(x + π/2): cosine is sine shifted left by a quarter period.
Amplitude A scales the height; the zeros of one fall at the peaks of the other.
